    11

    13	This module derives `Scheme.FiniteInAffine` from projectivity over an affine
    14	base. It does not construct a quasi-projectivity witness for any Picard scheme.

    25	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along open immersions. -/
    26	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    27	    [IsOpenImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    28	  classical
    29	  intro s hs
    30	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := hY (f.base '' s) (hs.image f.base)
    31	  letI : Fintype s := hs.fintype
    32	  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrle⟩ :=
    33	    AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
    34	      (fun x : s => f.base x)
    35	      (fun x => hU ⟨x, x.2, rfl⟩)
    36	      (fun x => Scheme.Hom.mem_opensRange.mpr ⟨(x : X), rfl⟩)
    37	  refine ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ Y.basicOpen r,
    38	    (U.2.basicOpen r).preimage_of_isOpenImmersion f hrle⟩, ?_⟩
    39	  intro x hx
    40	  change f.base x ∈ Y.basicOpen r
    41	  exact hr ⟨x, hx⟩

    46	  obtain ⟨Z, g₁, g₂, hg₁, hg₂, -⟩ :=

After an etale cover, represent the Picard class by an invertible sheaf and apply the fixed admissible translation, obtaining an invertible sheaf of degree \(n_{\mathrm{adm}}\). Its first cohomology vanishes by Theorem 1132, so its pushforward is locally free, commutes with base change, and has positive rank. The projective bundle of rank-one quotients of the dual pushforward is smooth and surjective over the test. It therefore has a section after a further etale cover. The corresponding nowhere-zero fibrewise section of the invertible sheaf cuts out a relative effective divisor whose translated Abel class is the original class.

     8	/-!
     9	# The overlap component of finite-stage Picard base change
    10	
    11	The overlaps produced by `Scheme.Pullback.gluing` are nested pullbacks. We first
    12	flatten that categorical presentation, using the certified pullback presentation of
    13	the original overlap, and then apply the existing affine overlap comparison.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	set_option autoImplicit false
    17	
    18	universe u
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    21	open scoped TensorProduct
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- Flatten the nested pullback obtained by first base-changing `U` and then
    28	intersecting it with `V`. The only input about `W` is its displayed pullback
    29	presentation as `U ×_X V`. -/
    30	noncomputable def nestedPullbackFlatteningIso
    31	    {U V X Y Z W : Scheme.{u}}
    32	    (iU : U ⟶ X) (iV : V ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    33	    (a : W ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ V)
    34	    (hab : a ≫ iU = b ≫ iV)
    35	    (hW : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk a b hab)) :
    36	    pullback (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV ≅
    37	      pullback (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g := by
    38	  let e : W ≅ pullback iU iV :=
    39	    hW.conePointUniqueUpToIso (pullback.isLimit iU iV)
    40	  have e_inv_fst : e.inv ≫ a = pullback.fst iU iV := by
    41	    change e.inv ≫ (PullbackCone.mk a b hab).fst = _
    42	    exact IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv_comp hW
    43	      (pullback.isLimit iU iV) WalkingCospan.left
    44	  exact
    45	    asIso (pullback.map
    46	      (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV
    47	      (pullback.snd g (iU ≫ f) ≫ iU) iV
    48	      (pullbackSymmetry (iU ≫ f) g).hom (𝟙 V) (𝟙 X)
    49	      (by simp) (by simp)) ≪≫
    50	    pullbackAssoc g (iU ≫ f) iU iV ≪≫
    51	    pullbackSymmetry g (pullback.fst iU iV ≫ (iU ≫ f)) ≪≫
    52	    asIso (pullback.map
    53	      (pullback.fst iU iV ≫ (iU ≫ f)) g
    54	      (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g
    55	      e.inv (𝟙 Y) (𝟙 Z)
    56	      (by
    57	        simpa only [Category.comp_id, Category.assoc] using
    58	          congrArg (fun q => q ≫ iU ≫ f) e_inv_fst.symm)
    59	      (by simp))
    60	
    61	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    62	/-- The first projection of the flattened pullback recovers the first projection
    63	of the inner pullback after composing with the first leg of the displayed overlap. -/
    64	@[reassoc]
    65	theorem nestedPullbackFlatteningIso_hom_comp_fst_comp_a
    66	    {U V X Y Z W : Scheme.{u}}
    67	    (iU : U ⟶ X) (iV : V ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    68	    (a : W ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ V)
    69	    (hab : a ≫ iU = b ≫ iV)
    70	    (hW : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk a b hab)) :
    71	    (nestedPullbackFlatteningIso iU iV f g a b hab hW).hom ≫
    72	        pullback.fst (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g ≫ a =
    73	      pullback.fst (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV ≫
    74	        pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g := by
    75	  let e : W ≅ pullback iU iV :=
    76	    hW.conePointUniqueUpToIso (pullback.isLimit iU iV)
    77	  have e_inv_fst : e.inv ≫ a = pullback.fst iU iV := by
    78	    change e.inv ≫ (PullbackCone.mk a b hab).fst = _
    79	    exact IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv_comp hW
    80	      (pullback.isLimit iU iV) WalkingCospan.left
    81	  simp only [nestedPullbackFlatteningIso, Iso.trans_hom, asIso_hom,
    82	    pullback.map, Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst_assoc,
    83	    pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_fst_assoc]
    84	  rw [e_inv_fst]
    85	  simp
    86	
    87	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
    88	/-- The first projection of the flattened pullback recovers the outer second
    89	projection after composing with the second leg of the displayed overlap. -/
    90	@[reassoc]
    91	theorem nestedPullbackFlatteningIso_hom_comp_fst_comp_b
    92	    {U V X Y Z W : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (iU : U ⟶ X) (iV : V ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    94	    (a : W ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ V)
    95	    (hab : a ≫ iU = b ≫ iV)
    96	    (hW : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk a b hab)) :
    97	    (nestedPullbackFlatteningIso iU iV f g a b hab hW).hom ≫
    98	        pullback.fst (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g ≫ b =
    99	      pullback.snd (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV := by
   100	  let e : W ≅ pullback iU iV :=
   101	    hW.conePointUniqueUpToIso (pullback.isLimit iU iV)
   102	  have e_inv_snd : e.inv ≫ b = pullback.snd iU iV := by
   103	    change e.inv ≫ (PullbackCone.mk a b hab).snd = _
   104	    exact IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_inv_comp hW
   105	      (pullback.isLimit iU iV) WalkingCospan.right
   106	  simp only [nestedPullbackFlatteningIso, Iso.trans_hom, asIso_hom,
   107	    pullback.map, Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst_assoc,
   108	    pullbackSymmetry_hom_comp_fst_assoc]
   109	  rw [e_inv_snd]
   110	  simp
   111	
   112	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
   113	/-- The second projection of the flattened pullback is the second projection of
   114	the inner pullback after the outer first projection. -/
   115	@[reassoc]
   116	theorem nestedPullbackFlatteningIso_hom_comp_snd
   117	    {U V X Y Z W : Scheme.{u}}
   118	    (iU : U ⟶ X) (iV : V ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
   119	    (a : W ⟶ U) (b : W ⟶ V)
   120	    (hab : a ≫ iU = b ≫ iV)
   121	    (hW : IsLimit (PullbackCone.mk a b hab)) :
   122	    (nestedPullbackFlatteningIso iU iV f g a b hab hW).hom ≫
   123	        pullback.snd (a ≫ iU ≫ f) g =
   124	      pullback.fst (pullback.fst (iU ≫ f) g ≫ iU) iV ≫
   125	        pullback.snd (iU ≫ f) g := by
   126	  simp [nestedPullbackFlatteningIso, pullback.map, Category.assoc]
   127	
   128	end
   129	
   130	end AlgebraicGeometry

   115	noncomputable def restrictionBaseChangeMap

   138	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in

   141	/-- The tensor-product and final-ring comparison for a chart, before applying

   143	noncomputable def chartRingBaseChangeIso

    31	/-- A quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme has a finite affine open cover with
    32	quasi-compact pairwise intersections. -/
    33	theorem Scheme.exists_finite_affineCover_inter_isQuasiCompact (X : Scheme.{u})
    34	    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    35	    ∃ s : Set X.affineOpens, s.Finite ∧ (⨆ i ∈ s, (i : X.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
    36	      ∀ U ∈ s, ∀ V ∈ s, IsCompact ((U : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X)) := by
    37	  obtain ⟨s, hs, he⟩ :=
    38	    (isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens (U := (⊤ : X.Opens))).mp
    39	      (by simpa using isCompact_univ (X := X))
    40	  refine ⟨s, hs, he.symm, ?_⟩
    41	  intro U _ V _
    42	  exact quasiSeparatedSpace_iff_forall_affineOpens.mp ‹_› U V
    43	
    44	/-- A finite affine presentation of the intersection of two affine opens.  Besides
    45	covering the intersection exactly, it records finite presentation of both restriction
    46	maps from the chart rings to every overlap-piece ring. -/
    47	structure Scheme.FiniteAffineOverlapPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    48	    (U V : X.affineOpens) where
    49	  pieces : Set X.affineOpens
    50	  finite_pieces : pieces.Finite
    51	  iSup_opens : (⨆ W ∈ pieces, (W : X.Opens)) = U.1 ⊓ V.1
    52	  piece_le_left : ∀ W ∈ pieces, W.1 ≤ U.1
    53	  piece_le_right : ∀ W ∈ pieces, W.1 ≤ V.1
    54	  leftRestriction_finitePresentation : ∀ W (hW : W ∈ pieces),
    55	    (X.homOfLE (piece_le_left W hW)).appTop.hom.FinitePresentation
    56	  rightRestriction_finitePresentation : ∀ W (hW : W ∈ pieces),
    57	    (X.homOfLE (piece_le_right W hW)).appTop.hom.FinitePresentation
    58	
    59	/-- A compact intersection of two affine opens admits a finite affine overlap
    60	presentation.  The two restriction maps are finitely presented because the inclusions
    61	of the affine overlap pieces into the affine charts are open immersions. -/
    62	noncomputable def Scheme.finiteAffineOverlapPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    63	    (U V : X.affineOpens) (h : IsCompact ((U : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X))) :
    64	    X.FiniteAffineOverlapPresentation U V := by
    65	  apply Classical.choice
    66	  obtain ⟨s, hs, he⟩ :=
    67	    (isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens (U := U.1 ⊓ V.1)).mp
    68	      (by simpa using h)
    69	  have hle (W : X.affineOpens) (hW : W ∈ s) : W.1 ≤ U.1 ⊓ V.1 := by
    70	    rw [he]
    71	    exact le_iSup_of_le W (le_iSup_of_le hW le_rfl)
    72	  refine ⟨
    73	    { pieces := s
    74	      finite_pieces := hs
    75	      iSup_opens := he.symm
    76	      piece_le_left := fun W hW => (hle W hW).trans inf_le_left
    77	      piece_le_right := fun W hW => (hle W hW).trans inf_le_right
    78	      leftRestriction_finitePresentation := ?_
    79	      rightRestriction_finitePresentation := ?_ }⟩
    80	  · intro W hW
    81	    exact (X.homOfLE ((hle W hW).trans inf_le_left)).finitePresentation_appTop
    82	  · intro W hW
    83	    exact (X.homOfLE ((hle W hW).trans inf_le_right)).finitePresentation_appTop

    10	
    11	Ported from the sibling Algebraic Jacobian project
    12	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover`).
    13	
    14	Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(L/K)` and let `X` be a
    15	scheme over `Spec L` with a semilinear `Γ`-action `ρ` (`SemilinearGalAction`).  This
    16	file discharges the gate `HasStableAffineCover` (the EGA II 4.5.4 pattern) from the
    17	orbit-in-affine hypothesis `ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen`: **every point of `X` has a
    18	`Γ`-stable affine open neighbourhood** (`hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`,
    19	registered as the sanctioned instance).  This is the geometric step `G2(a)` feeding
    20	the quotient gluing `G2(c)`; the deep gate `HasGaloisQuotient` is instance-free only for
    21	a **non-affine** total space — `Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean` discharges it
    22	globally under `[IsAffine X]`.

    24	## Pinned route (recorded before proving, per the campaign plan)
    25	
    26	Fix `x : X` with orbit inside the affine open `U` (the hypothesis; the orbit is
    27	finite because `Γ` is finite for finite-dimensional `L/K`).  Pin the **ambient open**
    28	`W := ⋂_γ (act γ)⁻¹ U` — a `Γ`-stable open (not necessarily affine) containing the
    29	orbit and contained in `U` (the `γ = 1` factor).
    30	
    31	1. **Prime avoidance** (`exists_mem_basicOpen_le_of_finite`, then transported into
    32	   the scheme by `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` bookkeeping in
    33	   `exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite`): there is `s ∈ Γ(X, U)` with
    34	   `orbit ⊆ D(s) ⊆ W`.  The algebraic heart is `Ideal.subset_union_prime`: the
    35	   vanishing ideal of `X \ W` in `Γ(X, U)` is not contained in the union of the
    36	   finitely many primes of the orbit points.
    37	2. **The norm** `N := ∏_γ γ(s)|_W ∈ Γ(X, W)`, where `γ(s) := (act γ).app U s` is the
    38	   section transport `Γ(X, U) → Γ(X, (act γ)⁻¹ U)`.  Then
    39	   `D(N) = ⋂_γ (act γ)⁻¹ D(s)`, by `D(product) = ⋂ D(factor)` and
    40	   `Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`.
    41	3. **Wall bypass (audit)**: `Γ`-stability of `D(N)` is proved at the level of
    42	   *opens*, never of sections: `(act τ)⁻¹ D(N) = ⋂_γ (act τ)⁻¹ (act γ)⁻¹ D(s)
    43	   = ⋂_γ (act (γτ))⁻¹ D(s) = D(N)` by preimage functoriality and reindexing the

    46	   section transport used is `Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`.  In particular no

     9	# Group schemes are separated (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1), Wave-5 X1)
    10	
    11	A group scheme over a field is separated: the diagonal
    12	`Δ : G ⟶ G ⊗ G` is the pullback of the unit section `η[G]` along the *difference map*
    13	`fst ⋅ snd⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G` ("`(x, y) ↦ x y⁻¹`"), and the unit section of a group scheme
    14	over a field is a closed immersion (mathlib, `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`), so
    15	the diagonal is a closed immersion by stability under base change.
    16	
    17	Stated as reusable infrastructure, in three layers:
    18	
    19	* `CategoryTheory.GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal` — the purely categorical half, for a group
    20	  object in ANY cartesian monoidal category: the square
    21	
    22	  ```
    23	        G ------ lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G) -----> G ⊗ G
    24	        |                                  |
    25	     toUnit G                       fst G G * (snd G G)⁻¹
    26	        |                                  |
    27	        v                                  v
    28	      𝟙_ C ---------- η[G] -------------> G
    29	  ```
    30	
    31	  is a pullback (the Hom-group calculus of `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian`
    32	  does all the work).
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one` — a group scheme over an
    34	  ARBITRARY base scheme whose unit section is a closed immersion is separated.  Note:
    35	  no finiteness hypothesis whatsoever (`LocallyOfFiniteType` is NOT needed).
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_of_grpObj` (instance) — over a field the closed-
    37	  immersion hypothesis is mathlib's instance, so every group scheme over a field is
    38	  separated.
    39	
    40	The Wave-5 datum corollary `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.isSeparated` closes the
    41	file: `d.J.hom` is separated for every Jacobian datum `d` — one of the two inputs of
    42	the properness assembly P3 (`IsProper = IsSeparated + UniversallyClosed + lft`).
    43	-/

    58	/-- **The diagonal of a group object is the pullback of the unit along the difference
    59	map** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1), categorical half): for a group object `G` in a cartesian
    60	monoidal category, the square with top `Δ = lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)`, left `toUnit G`, right
    61	the difference map `fst ⋅ snd⁻¹ : G ⊗ G ⟶ G`, and bottom the unit `η[G]` is a
    62	pullback.  Here `⋅`/`⁻¹` are the Hom-group operations on `G ⊗ G ⟶ G` (scoped in
    63	`CategoryTheory.MonObj`), so the difference map is `lift (fst G G) (snd G G ≫ ι) ≫ μ`
    64	definitionally. -/
    65	theorem GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal (G : C) [GrpObj G] :
    66	    IsPullback (toUnit G) (lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)) η[G] (fst G G * (snd G G)⁻¹) where
    67	  w := by
    68	    rw [MonObj.comp_mul, GrpObj.comp_inv, lift_fst, lift_snd, mul_inv_cancel, Hom.one_def]
    69	  isLimit' := Nonempty.intro <| PullbackCone.IsLimit.mk _
    70	    (fun s => s.snd ≫ fst G G)
    71	    (fun s => toUnit_unique _ _)
    72	    (fun s => by
    73	      -- the cone condition says `(s.snd ≫ fst) ⋅ (s.snd ≫ snd)⁻¹ = 1` in the Hom-group
    74	      have key : s.snd ≫ fst G G = s.snd ≫ snd G G := by

    78	        exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp h

    81	      have := hm₂ =≫ fst G G
    82	      simpa using this)
    83

    90	/-- **A group scheme with closed unit section is separated** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)):
    91	for a group object `G` of `Over S`, `S` any base scheme, if the unit section
    92	`η[G].left : S ⟶ G.left` is a closed immersion then `G.hom` is separated.  The
    93	diagonal is the base change of `η[G].left` along the difference map
    94	(`GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal`, pushed to schemes by `Over.forget`), and closed
    95	immersions are stable under base change.  No finiteness hypothesis is needed. -/
    96	theorem isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Over S) [GrpObj G]
    97	    [IsClosedImmersion η[G].left] : IsSeparated G.hom := by
    98	  constructor
    99	  have sq := (GrpObj.isPullback_diagonal G).map (Over.forget S)
   100	  have h : IsClosedImmersion (lift (𝟙 G) (𝟙 G)).left :=
   101	    MorphismProperty.of_isPullback sq ‹IsClosedImmersion η[G].left›
   102	  exact h
   103	
   104	/-- **A group scheme over a field is separated** (Kleiman `lem:agps`(1)): the unit
   105	section is a closed immersion by mathlib's group-scheme instance
   106	(`AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`), and `isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one`
   107	applies.  No `LocallyOfFiniteType` hypothesis is needed. -/
   108	instance isSeparated_of_grpObj {K : Type u} [Field K] (G : Over (Spec (.of K)))
   109	    [GrpObj G] : IsSeparated G.hom :=
   110	  isSeparated_of_isClosedImmersion_one G

   115	theorem JacobianData.isSeparated {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   116	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   117	    (d : JacobianData C) : IsSeparated d.J.hom :=
   118	  letI := d.grpObj

    10	/-!
    11	# Orbit affineness for the finite-stage Picard glue
    12	
    13	A projective finite-stage glued representative has the finite-in-affine property, so every
    14	orbit of its canonical finite-Galois action lies in an affine open.  This file records that
    15	producer at the exact carrier `P.gluedOver` used by finite-stage descent.
    16	
    17	The projectivity argument is deliberately explicit.  The affine-chart glue package does not
    18	yet construct `P.gluedMap.IsProjective`; that geometric certificate remains the sole input of
    19	this bridge rather than being hidden in an auxiliary class.
    20	-/
    21

    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

events.text:
Read-only investigation complete; no edits or full builds were run.

**Carrier And Charts**

- `P.glueData` is constructed by `pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData` in [Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage.lean:97).
- There is no separate project definition `P.glued`; the carrier is `P.glueData.glued`.
- `P.gluedMap : P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1)` is the multicoequalizer descent of the chart structure maps, and `P.gluedOver := Over.mk P.gluedMap`, in [Pic0FiniteStageGluedOver.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageGluedOver.lean:38).
- The finite chart index is the subtype of the chosen atlas, with a `Finite` instance, in [Pic0FiniteStageAffineIntersections.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageAffineIntersections.lean:33).
- Chart and overlap model rings are `Pic0FiniteStageModelRing ... (Sum.inl U)` and `... (Sum.inr (U,V))`, respectively, in [Pic0FiniteStageTripleOverlapRings.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageTripleOverlapRings.lean:336).
- Final chart rings are
  `P.N.1 ⊗[P.M.1] Pic0FiniteStageChartModelRing ... U`; overlaps are the analogous tensor products.
- Each `P.glueData.ι U` is an open immersion, hence an immersion. Its composite with the structure map is exactly the corresponding affine `Spec.map`, by [Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChange.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChange.lean:37).

**Available Geometry**

No `Pic0FiniteStage*.lean` theorem currently proves `IsProper P.gluedMap`, `QuasiCompact P.gluedMap`, `LocallyOfFiniteType P.gluedMap`, or a global projective-space immersion. The existing `[IsProper C.hom]` assumptions concern the input curve.

Two useful facts are nevertheless directly derivable:

- `LocallyOfFiniteType P.gluedMap`: chart model rings have finite-presentation instances, preserved by both scalar extensions. Apply `IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover` and rewrite with `glueData_ι_gluedMap`. The exact pattern is [JacobianDataCharts.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:151).
- `QuasiCompact P.gluedMap`: the chart index is finite and every chart is affine/compact, so `P.glueData.openCover.compactSpace` gives compactness of the glued carrier. The pattern is [JacobianDataCharts.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:161).

Given the existing `rep`, `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` also puts a group-object structure on `P.gluedOver`, after which `isSeparated_of_grpObj` supplies `IsSeparated P.gluedMap`. Properness still lacks the genuinely new `UniversallyClosed` argument.

**Exact P7 Gap**

AJCR’s [finiteInAffine_of_isImmersion](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:43) means p7 needs only an underlying-scheme immersion
```lean
P.glueData.glued ⟶ ℙ(n; Spec (.of P.N.1))
```
for finite `n`. It need not be closed or proper. H-quasi-projectivity is a convenient packaged certificate, not a required port.

To prove `P.gluedMap.IsProjective`, the immersion must additionally be closed; alternatively, [of_isProper_of_immersion](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Projective/ProjectiveMorphism.lean:97) reduces this to properness plus the immersion.

The closest direct group result, `finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible`, requires an algebraically closed base and irreducible carrier, neither available at the finite Galois stage. A general finite-type-group-scheme quasi-projectivity/`FiniteInAffine` theorem is therefore the shortest conceptual bridge.

The base-change files only identify individual charts and overlaps and identify the global pullback with the gluing of pulled-back charts. They do not assemble an isomorphism to the exact Picard carrier; [Pic0CriticalPath.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0CriticalPath.lean:284) explicitly records this and orbit/projectivity as missing.

Commit `5ee5a7f349` adds only conditional consumers: `Pic0FiniteStageOrbitAffine` converts a supplied `hproj` to `FiniteInAffine`, and `Pic0FiniteStageStableAffineCover` consumes that result. It adds no projectivity producer.
